clue.text: Cycling mayor's on board to make cuts

definitions.note: a noun phrase: shanks are improvised knives, things used to make cuts

indicators.note: on as in being aboard: the cycled mayor sits within the board's two letters

parts.note: SS, steamship, the vessel boarded

indicators.note: cycling moves the first letter of the mayor's name round to the end

parts.note: Sadiq Khan is the Mayor of London

explanation.surface: A London mayor famous for his bike scheme is apparently on a board deciding where budgets get trimmed.
explanation.walkthrough: The board is a ship, SS for steamship. Boris Johnson is the mayor known for cycling; this is Sadiq Khan, whose name 'Cycling' turns into HANK.
explanation.definitionFit: Shanks is slang, especially prison slang, for homemade stabbing blades, the tools a person uses to slash.

clue.text: Superior nosh must be demolished with bibs

indicators.note: food that is demolished is wolfed down and broken up, so these letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A snooty diner insists the meal be eaten wearing bibs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must be demolished' rearranges NOSH and BIBS together.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone snobbish behaves as if superior to others; the adjective in its haughty sense.

clue.text: Stripping off, one with the hump needs air con fixed — not a cold drink!

indicators.note: stripping off the outer layer takes away the first and last letters of the humped animal

parts.note: a camel is the animal with a hump

indicators.note: an air-con unit that is fixed is reworked, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone sulking and undressing in the heat wants the air conditioning repaired, and refuses an iced drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stripping off' leaves AME from CAMEL; 'fixed' rearranges AIR CON into RICANO. 'With the hump' looks like British slang for being in a sulk, but it is a camel.
explanation.definitionFit: An americano is espresso topped with hot water, a coffee served hot, so a drink that is not cold.

clue.text: How a script's list of characters might describe 14 before line for actress

parts.words: How a script's list of characters might describe 14
parts.note: 14 is Sir Keir Starmer, so a play's cast list might style him 'Keir, a knight'
a ley line is an alignment of ancient sites, so ley means line

explanation.surface: A puzzle about how a playscript's dramatis personae would introduce a politician, then a line, giving a film star.
explanation.walkthrough: Cast lists describe characters briefly, as in 'Keir, a knight'; Starmer was knighted in 2014. 'before' simply orders the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Keira Knightley is the English film actress of Pride and Prejudice and Pirates of the Caribbean.

clue.text: Mediums in which Korean rapper's describing a certain style

indicators.note: describing in its sense of drawing round, so the rapper's letters encircle the style

parts.note: Psy is the South Korean rapper of Gangnam Style, plus the S of the possessive
chic is a particular stylish elegance

explanation.surface: A question about which spiritualists a Korean rapper mentions while describing a fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'describing' means drawing a line round, as one describes a circle. Psy's hit was Gangnam Style, which 'a certain style' slyly evokes.
explanation.definitionFit: Mediums are people who claim to contact spirits, which is what psychics claim too.

clue.text: Good man presented with gold, silver and lead in enigmatic caskets?

parts.note: ST, saint, the crossword good man
or is gold in heraldry
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

indicators.note: the lead in a word is its first letter, so only the start of enigmatic is taken

explanation.surface: A suitor faces the riddling gold, silver and lead caskets of The Merchant of Venice.
explanation.walkthrough: In Shakespeare's Merchant of Venice Portia's suitors choose among gold, silver and lead caskets, so 'lead' reads as a metal but is the first-letter signal. The question mark marks caskets as one example of storage.
explanation.definitionFit: Caskets are small boxes for keeping valuables, one instance of containers for keeping things.

clue.text: Film exec secures silence over papers

indicators.note: the executive holds the other piece firmly inside it

parts.note: a CEO is the chief executive

indicators.note: over in a down clue turns the quiet spell upside down, so it is read backwards

parts.note: a lull is a period of quiet
ID, identity papers

explanation.surface: A studio boss hushes things up over some documents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns the silence upwards, as this is a down clue, giving LLUL; 'secures' holds it inside the boss.
explanation.definitionFit: Celluloid is the old plastic base of cinema film stock, and stands for the movies themselves.

clue.text: Spaniard's English doesn't include special term for fireplace

indicators.note: the word leaves out a letter it would otherwise contain

parts.note: inglés is the Spanish word for English

explanation.surface: A Spanish speaker's English lacks a particular word for a hearth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doesn't include' drops the S from INGLES; 'term for' is the link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingle is an old word for a hearth or domestic fire, as in inglenook.

clue.text: Some blushes at explicit stuff

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Something about racy material that makes people blush.
explanation.definitionFit: To sate is to stuff with food until fully satisfied; both are verbs of filling up.

clue.text: Where you may find US health care even more ridiculous

parts.note: the answer to where: in an ...
ER, the emergency room of an American hospital

explanation.surface: A jibe that American health care gets ever more absurd.
explanation.walkthrough: The question is answered 'in an ER'; ER is the American term for a hospital's emergency department.
explanation.definitionFit: Inane means silly or senseless, so the comparative is sillier still.

clue.text: Old bishop and priest giving us daggers

parts.note: B, bishop in chess notation
Eli is the priest who raised Samuel in the Bible

explanation.surface: A churchman and a cleric are glaring at us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'giving us daggers' suggests hostile looks, but the daggers are printers' marks.
explanation.definitionFit: Obeli, plural of obelus, are the dagger symbols printers use to mark footnotes.

clue.text: Twisted version of Noël featured in dark display

indicators.note: featured in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: night is the dark

indicators.note: a twisted version is a distorted form, so the Christmas word's letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, without the accent

explanation.surface: A garish take on a Christmas carol in a dark show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twisted version of' rearranges the Christmas word to EONL, and 'featured in' sets that inside the dark.
explanation.definitionFit: A neon light is an illuminated sign or tube, used in advertising signs and shop-window shows.

clue.text: One representing our bit of land might make it an Airbnb briefly

definitions.text: One representing our bit of land

indicators.note: the letters could be remade into the answer, a rearrangement
briefly cuts the word short by its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone muses that a short-let flat could be rebranded as our island home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' leaves AIRBN from AIRBNB; 'might make' rearranges IT, AN and AIRBN.
explanation.definitionFit: Britannia is the helmeted female figure personifying Great Britain, its national emblem.

clue.text: Having entered the Indy 500, European is exhausted

indicators.note: the European goes inside the other letters

parts.note: the Independent, nicknamed the Indy, publishes this crossword, so it is us
D is 500 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A European racer, having joined the Indianapolis 500, is worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: The Indy 500 is an American motor race, but 'the Indy' here is the Independent newspaper, i.e. US, and 500 is D.
explanation.definitionFit: Used up and exhausted both mean consumed until nothing is left.

clue.text: See 22
Sailor damaged a chart with rum

indicators.note: a damaged chart is spoilt, so these letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A seafarer ruined a map by spilling rum on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' rearranges A CHART and RUM; 'rum' looks like another anagram word but is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Dame Ellen MacArthur is the English yachtswoman who set a solo round-the-world record.

clue.text: I'm disgusted by experimental musician — change the record!

parts.note: Brian Eno is an ambient and experimental composer
ugh is the exclamation of disgust

explanation.surface: A listener, sick of an avant-garde record, begs for something else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' just sets the two pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'change the record!' to someone is telling them to stop harping on, as an exasperated 'enough!' does.

clue.text: Traffic rising on URLs leading to site for swingers

indicators.note: rising in a down clue reads the word upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: to traffic is to deal in or sell, as to flog does
web addresses are links

explanation.surface: Web traffic increasing on links that point to a site for partner-swappers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns FLOG upwards to GOLF. The swingers are golfers, not the adult sense the surface hints at.
explanation.definitionFit: A golf links is a course, the place where golfers swing their clubs.

clue.text: Fellows regularly glimpsed Rhett and O'Hara in first half of Oscar-winning film

indicators.note: in puts the glimpsed letters inside the half title
takes only the opening half of the film's title

parts.note: Ben-Hur won eleven Oscars in 1960

indicators.note: only every other letter of each name is seen

explanation.surface: Gone With the Wind's lovers turn up in an Oscar winner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly glimpsed' gives RET from Rhett and HR from O'Hara; these go 'in' BEN, the 'first half of' Ben-Hur. Rhett Butler and Scarlett O'Hara suggest Gone With the Wind, a red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: Brethren are brothers in a fellowship, members of a society or religious order.

clue.text: EastEnders matriarch gives up tons for a million Twitter followers?

indicators.note: the matriarch's name surrenders some letters
for here means in exchange for, swapping one set of letters for another

parts.note: Dot Cotton was the long-running matriarch in the BBC soap EastEnders
T and TON are both abbreviations of ton, so together they make the plural
M is a million

explanation.surface: A soap star quits for a mass of social media fans.
explanation.walkthrough: EastEnders is a long-running BBC soap. 'gives up' and 'for' replace TTON (T plus TON) with M.
explanation.definitionFit: In the web address twitter.com, the part that follows the site name is the .com suffix.

clue.text: Neither songs nor stories will employ independent contractors

indicators.note: neither ... will employ says the first word does without a letter
with neither, says the letter is not employed by either word

parts.note: music means songs

indicators.note: nor carries the same refusal to employ over to the second word

parts.note: lies are tall stories

explanation.surface: A union-style complaint that musicians and storytellers won't hire freelancers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neither ... nor ... will employ independent' removes I from both MUSIC and LIES. Contractors here are things that contract, not hired workers.
explanation.definitionFit: Muscles work by contracting, so they are literally things that contract.

clue.text: Spin round to disorientate canoeist

indicators.note: round says the spin letters go round the other piece

parts.note: PR, public relations, is spin
to addle is to muddle or confuse

explanation.surface: Whirling a kayaker round to make them dizzy.
explanation.walkthrough: Spin looks like physical whirling, but it is media spin, public relations; 'round' wraps it about the muddling.
explanation.definitionFit: A paddler propels a canoe with a paddle, as a canoeist does.

clue.text: Old man Methuselah's spoken of as a man of 20

definitions.note: 20 is MUSCLES, so a man of muscles

parts.note: pop is a father, the old man

indicators.note: spoken of says the word said out loud is spelt differently in the grid

parts.note: Methuselah is the setter, who refers to himself as I; the 's is is

explanation.surface: The setter, who shares his name with the oldest man in the Bible, is described as a muscleman.
explanation.walkthrough: Crossword setters often refer to themselves as I or me; I sounds like EYE. 20 is MUSCLES, and Popeye's spinach-powered muscles are famous.
explanation.definitionFit: Popeye the Sailor is the cartoon hero whose forearms bulge after eating spinach, a muscle man.

clue.text: Lawyer turned politician to direct justice system, says Spooner

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words

parts.note: to steer is to direct
karma is the cosmic system of just deserts

explanation.surface: A former barrister in government aims to steer the courts.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of 'steer karma' gives Keir Starmer; the swap is by sound, not spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Keir Starmer was a barrister and Director of Public Prosecutions before becoming Labour leader.

clue.text: English student gets one over on cross novelist

parts.note: L, learner, the student on L-plates
I is the Roman numeral one
O is the cricket abbreviation for over
a cross is T-shaped

explanation.surface: A literature student scores a point against an angry author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' looks like angry but is the T shape; 'gets' and 'on' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: George Eliot was the pen name of Mary Ann Evans, author of Middlemarch.

clue.text: One of many youngsters certain to pinch pennies ahead of rising rent

indicators.note: the first word holds the other letter tightly, as if pinching it

parts.note: set means fixed or certain
P stands for pence, pennies
up means rising
to let is to rent out

explanation.surface: A landlord is sure to save money ahead of putting the rent up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to pinch' puts P inside SET, making SEPT; 'pinch pennies' reads as being stingy.
explanation.definitionFit: A septuplet is one of seven children born together, a very large multiple birth.

clue.text: Free tips from parents' siblings ignored

indicators.note: the tips are the two end letters of the word
the end letters are ignored, dropped from the word

parts.note: aunties are your parents' sisters

explanation.surface: Advice from aunts and uncles that nobody followed, given free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tips from ... ignored' drops A and S from AUNTIES. 'Tips' looks like advice.
explanation.definitionFit: To untie is to undo knots, to set loose or release.

clue.text: Hide after dropping trendy basin

indicators.note: in a down clue the trendy letters drop to the bottom of the word

parts.note: a sink is a basin
in means fashionable

explanation.surface: Concealing something after letting a fashionable washbasin fall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping' moves IN from the middle of SINK down to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal's hide is its skin, a noun sense, rather than the verb conceal.

clue.text: See 3
Who may change a few notes for a grand

definitions.text: Who may change a few notes for a grand

parts.words: Who may change a few notes for a grand
parts.note: reads like a money changer swapping banknotes for a thousand pounds, but it is a piano expert adjusting a grand piano's off-key notes

explanation.surface: Someone who would swap some banknotes for a thousand pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: A grand is slang for a thousand pounds and notes are banknotes, but here the grand is a piano.
explanation.definitionFit: A piano tuner adjusts strings so the notes sound true, working on a grand piano among others.

clue.text: Sign off on another order coming from señorita's quarters

indicators.note: the pieces are put in a different order, a rearrangement
the word is cut into four two-letter quarters, SE NO RI TA, and those are reordered

parts.note: taken as written, without the accent; the 's is the possessive

explanation.surface: A young Spanish woman's suggestion of a fresh instruction to be approved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another order coming from ... quarters' splits SENORITA into SE, NO, RI, TA and rearranges those blocks.
explanation.definitionFit: To notarise a document is to have a notary certify it, formally signing it off.

clue.text: Into which Icarus fell and — they say — what caused that fall?

parts.note: in Greek myth Icarus plunged into the sea when his wax wings melted

indicators.note: they say means the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: the sun melted the wax on Icarus's wings

explanation.surface: A question about the myth of Icarus: where he fell and what brought him down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fall' seems to continue the myth but is the American word for autumn.
explanation.definitionFit: Fall is the American name for autumn, one of the four times of year.
